writeup.headline: Zoom rates Hold at 64, one point below Buy, as strong cash generation offsets slow growth.
writeup.thesis: Zoom scores 64, just one point under the Buy line, held back mainly by modest growth: TTM revenue growth of 5.0%, with growth slowed by 0.5 pp from the previous quarter. Quality and the balance sheet carry the score: a 77.3% gross margin, a 38.6% FCF margin, diluted share count down 2.8% year on year, and net cash with no debt. Valuation is middling. In absolute terms the stock trades at 6.0x sales, 15.6x FCF and 19.2x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 1.4 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, and overall it sits near the middle of its own history. The trend and news factors are mildly positive. The price is 9.0% above its 200-day average but shares are 4.4 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, and new long-term targets and product launches at Zoomtopia are partly offset by insider selling.
key_risks: Low single-digit revenue growth could slow further from TTM revenue growth of 5.0%.
Stock-based compensation is 14.6% of revenue, which weighs on underlying profitability.
P/S is more expensive than at 48 of the last 61 month-ends.
Competition from Microsoft Teams and other AI collaboration tools could pressure pricing and growth.
An early-stage BIPA class action over AI Companion voiceprints could add legal costs.
what_would_change: A gain of just 1 point would move the rating to Buy, for example from re-accelerating revenue growth that lifts the growth score of 42.
Better relative price performance against SPY and QQQ would lift the trend score of 57 and could tip the rating to Buy.
A fall to Sell would need a 20-point drop, such as a sharp growth decline combined with worsening news or margins.
